body:
# Independent audit: residual-program KKT, martingale dual, and cap loads


`candidate 99d50c87eb055f05`.


In particular contact-weighted volume is not ordinary total mixed mass,
and destinations of the transport need not be obstacle contacts. No
numeric premise or unconditional residual-budget bound is used.

## 1. KKT existence and all signs

The primal feasible set is a finite polyhedron, and attainment was
independently audited in `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.
At an optimizer every direction satisfying the active linear constraints
is feasible for a sufficiently small positive step: there are only
finitely many inactive positive slacks. Differentiating the objective
along these directions and applying finite Farkas separation gives
nonnegative multipliers on the active inequalities. The extension
sum(h_i)_+^q is differentiable at zero for q>1; for q=1 the objective
is linear. Thus no constraint qualification or omitted zero-node
derivative is needed.

The h_i derivative has signs

    s_i-lambda_i+out_i-in_i=0,

and the g_i derivative is the outgoing base moment
sum_j mu_ij(p_j-p_i)=0. Complementarity on interpolation edges, summed
against those row moments, gives sum_ij mu_ij(h_i-h_j)=0. Therefore
sum lambda_i e_i=sum lambda_i h_i=sum s_i h_i=qR. Summing the same
flow balance gives equal total lambda and s mass; multiplying by
base coordinates and using row moments gives equal first moments.
All source signs in (3)--(7) check.

## 2. Zero nodes and the explicit absorbing transport

For q>1, a zero-height row can send positive mu only to another
zero-height node: the row's complemented interpolation equation is
sum_j mu_ij h_j=0. Summing the balance over all zero nodes gives
their nonnegative total lambda equal to minus their incoming flow
from positive nodes. Both must vanish. The remaining internal flow
is conservative and has row barycenters. Consequently its summed
squared edge displacement is zero, using

    sum_j mu_ij |p_j-p_i|^2
      =sum_j mu_ij (|p_j|^2-|p_i|^2)

and global conservation. Distinct indices are distinct bases, so
every internal off-diagonal mu vanishes. Removing zero nodes is
therefore exact, not an approximation to a possibly recurrent class.

On the remaining finite nodes, a_i=s_i+out_i>0 and
T_ij=mu_ij/a_i has every row sum strictly below one, uniformly by
a positive finite minimum s_i/a_i. Hence N=(I-T)^(-1) exists as a
convergent nonnegative geometric series. In row notation the balance
is a=lambda+aT, so lambda N=a. The row-sum and row-barycenter
identities are respectively

    (I-T)1=D1,       (I-T)p=Dp.

Thus pi=diag(lambda) N D has row masses lambda, column masses s,
and each source row has the exact barycenter of its source base.
This checks the orientation of the inverse and both diagonal factors.
For q=1 all s_i=1, including at zero heights, so the same construction
works directly without removing them.

Primal interpolation makes every claimed supporting-plane gap
nonnegative. Its pi integral is
sum s_j h_j-sum lambda_i h_i=0, with the source-row mean canceling
the slope terms. Every positive pi edge therefore has zero gap.
No assertion that its target also satisfies h=e follows, or is used.

## 3. Exact dual and attainment

For any nonnegative row-martingale matrix, Jensen's inequality for
an interpolating convex threshold gives
sum lambda_i e_i<=sum s_j h_j. The convex conjugate of h^q on
h>=0 is (q-1)q^(-q/(q-1)) s^(q/(q-1)) for s>=0, giving the exact
weak-duality constant in (12). For q=1, prescribed unit column sums
give weak duality directly. The constructed pi has column masses
s_j=q h_j^(q-1) and input reward qR, so conjugacy is equality and
its objective is precisely R. This proves strong duality and
attainment without an unverified minimax exchange.

For q>1 coercivity can also be checked explicitly: with total mass
L, the reward is at most (max e_i)L, whereas
sum_j s_j^q'>=N^(1-q') L^q'. The negative term dominates as
L tends to infinity. For q=1 the unit columns give a compact
feasible set. Neither argument prescribes missing row masses.

An exact small calibration confirms the source/target convention.
For bases 0,1,2, q=2, and obstacle e=(0,1,0), an optimum is
h=(1,1,1), with s=(2,2,2), lambda=(0,6,0), and only
mu_(1,0)=mu_(1,2)=2. The coupling sends mass 2 from base 1
to EACH of bases 0,1,2. Its reward is 6 and its conjugate
penalty is 3, giving R=3. The endpoint destinations are not
obstacle contacts. These data are realized, for example, by
constant unit fibers on the complete base {0,1,2} and the two
vertical caps isolating the endpoint fibers; this cap family
does not cover the middle fiber and is used only as a transport
calibration, not as a covering-family claim.

## 4. Actual cap loads

Positive-lambda sources are contacts. For q>1 they have strictly
positive heights by the zero-node argument, so
rho_i=lambda_i/(q e_i^(q-1)) is defined. For q=1 rho=lambda
is defined even at zero residual. Euler's equality gives exactly
R=sum rho_i e_i^q and hence the identity involving the actual
captured volumes c_i^*=V_i-e_i^q.

For a fixed original cap a, summing its trace at contact bases with
weights rho_i is at most L_a times that cap's full actual mixed
mass, where L_a is the maximum of precisely the relevant rho_i.
Applying the union bound separately at each contact gives (16),
and the actual common cap budget gives (17). No sum of maxima has
been replaced by the parity count, and no contact weight has been
discarded. For a genuinely covering family, the intrinsic centroid
Grünbaum bound at each fiber supplies a cap capturing at least
gamma_q V_i, hence the stated contact-weighted residual inequality.
It does not change the contact-weighted volume to M.

## 5. Midpoint and conditional row equalities

If two same-parity contacts have positive residual roots, EVERY
allowed residual set has positive q-volume at both bases. Their
Minkowski midpoint lies in the actual integer midpoint residual.
Different endpoint direction spaces would make that midpoint
dimension greater than q, impossible by the definition of the
largest integer fiber dimension. They therefore have a common
q-dimensional direction space, and intrinsic Brunn--Minkowski
applies. Taking the finite minimum of its root bound and comparing
with the convex threshold gives the exact equality chain (18).
Thus the midpoint is again a positive contact, and equality in
convexity makes the threshold affine on the whole joining segment.

For a residual subset active at the midpoint, equality forces it
active at both endpoints and forces Brunn--Minkowski equality.
For q>=2 the positive-volume closures are homothetic; for q=1
they are intervals. Their Minkowski midpoint is contained in the
middle residual closure and has equal full q-volume, so the two
convex bodies agree. Their centroids consequently average exactly.
Closing these bounded positive-dimensional convex residuals changes
neither volume nor centroid.

The corresponding martingale-row claim correctly retains the
hypothesis that EVERY positive target is a positive obstacle
contact. Their weighted average threshold equals the source height
by the supporting-plane identity. A source-active residual then
gives equality through the weighted Brunn--Minkowski chain. The
integer source again rules out incompatible direction spaces.
Without the target-contact premise the proof would fail, and the
source explicitly does not make that extension.

Finally (19) follows by paying at least (1-eta)V_p of captured
volume on each indicated base. A zero residual volume may describe
a nonempty lower-dimensional set; the source does not confuse it
with nonemptiness needed for a later Minkowski argument.

No correction was needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
